Personnel Dossier • The Manning Family Orchestra (1981–Present)

The Residents of The Hollow Square

Before Fractured Prisms debuted in 1983, they were a six-piece family ensemble—the Manning Family Orchestra. After a sudden freezing-fog white-out and black-ice pileup on the M6 motorway over Shap Fell in Cumbria in the winter of 1981 claimed four members of their generation, surviving siblings Claire and Rhys Manning carried their family's salvaged instruments across the Atlantic to Williamsport, Maryland to build The Fragile Fortress.

The Surviving Vanguard (Romford, UK → Williamsport & Hagerstown, MD)

1. The Surviving Siblings

Older Sister • Age 22 in 1983 Lead Vocals & Gwen's Wooden Flute

Claire Manning (“The Voice in the Fog”)

Claire has lived with cerebral palsy her entire life (navigating the world from a manual wheelchair) and is autistic (highly verbal), experiencing intense sensory depth and nighttime terrors. Teaching herself to play her late cousin Gwen's salvaged wooden concert flute on “Mirrors of Yesterday” and “The Hollow Square,” Claire breathes living acoustic warmth into the center of Rhys's mechanical synthesizer fortress.

📖 Open Claire Manning Dossier →
Younger Brother • Age 20 in 1983 Synthesizers, Sequencers & Safe Person

Rhys Manning (“The Mechanical Heart”)

Neurotypical and without physical disabilities, Rhys has been Claire's 24/7 caretaker, anchor, and ultimate safe person since childhood in their accessible Romford home. Refusing to hire studio session musicians to replace their lost family, Rhys programmed towering banks of Roland and Yamaha synthesizers and LinnDrum percussion while playing Julian's Rickenbacker bass and Simon's guitars himself.

📖 Open Rhys Manning Dossier →
In Memoriam • Winter 1981 M6 Shap Fell Motorway Disaster (Cumbria, UK)

2. The Missing Four of the Manning Family Orchestra

Every synthesizer patch, drum sequence, and acoustic passage on Carnaby Street (1983) and 1883 (1984) is engineered to preserve the musical voices of the four family members lost on the M6 at Shap Fell.

Cousin • Woodwinds Oboe, Clarinet & Wooden Concert Flute

Gwen Manning — The Soul of “Safe Harbor”

Before every family performance, Gwen played a centering woodwind melody she called “Safe Harbor” to calm Claire's sensory nerves. Her wooden concert flute—the very first instrument the family ever purchased—was pulled intact from the 1981 M6 wreckage and remains Claire's most sacred possession.

Older Brother • Percussionist Acoustic Drums, Gongs & Orchestral Chimes

Alistair Manning — The Heartbeat

Alistair commanded a sprawling acoustic drum kit surrounded by gongs and orchestral chimes. Rhys's relentless, mathematical 1983 LinnDrum programming and massive gated-reverb snare hits on “A Prophecy Unfolds” and “The Hollow Square” were built to mechanically reconstruct Alistair's pulse.

Cousin • Low-End Foundation Rickenbacker Bass Guitar & Classical Cello

Julian Hayes — The Deep Architecture

Julian wove rich, cinematic low-end counter-melodies on cello and Rickenbacker bass. Inside the Williamsport studio, Rhys plays Julian's actual salvaged Rickenbacker bass and pairs it with sweeping fretless bass synthesizers.

Cousin • Lead Guitars Acoustic & Electric Six-String Guitars

Simon Hayes — The Soaring Vanguard

Architect of the family orchestra's soaring guitar solos. Rhys straps on Simon's actual guitars using Simon's old picks and loops them into his sequencers, while on “Mirrors of Yesterday,” Claire replaces what would have been Simon's guitar solo with a breathtaking wooden flute solo.

Production Infrastructure • Hagerstown, MD & Soho, London

3. The Hagerstown 70mm Soundstage & The Soho Mail-Drop Decoy

Apex Industrial Holdings • Hagerstown, MD

The 35mm / 70mm Victorian Soundstage

Inside an unassuming corrugated metal hangar in a Hagerstown industrial park, Rhys and Claire constructed a permanent 360-degree 1883 Victorian London set of The Hollow Square complete with whisper-quiet hydraulic lifts hidden behind the walls. Shooting on 35mm and 70mm film rather than video tape, they used in-camera optical double-exposures and pneumatic self-playing drums so the Missing Four appeared as translucent spectral presences beside them.

Transatlantic Privacy Shield • Soho, London

The Soho Mail-Drop Decoy & Route 441

To keep British tabloid press and warring fan factions (“The Hampstead Heath Purists” vs. “The Moors Exiles”) convinced the band was hiding in an English manor, all fan mail was routed through a rented P.O. Box in Soho, London and air-freighted in bulk to Washington County, Maryland—allowing Claire and Rhys to ride the Route 441 County Commuter bus between Williamsport and Hagerstown in complete peace.

Engine Room Records (Real-World Imprint)

In real life, Engine Room Records (never “Engine Room Records, LLC”) is the creative brand and private record imprint under which Michael P. Ragsdale produces and distributes his music.
